title: THE MYSTERY OF INIQUITY
mv: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only He who now restrains will do so until He is taken out of the way.
mvp: “For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only He who now restrains will do so until He is taken out of the way.” 2Thessalonians 2:7 (NKJV)
assignment: Mention five (5) aspects of the world system capable of luring you into being a perpetual sinner e.g. Clubbing etc. (2x5=10 marks).

b.x: Mystery simply means something that baffles understanding and cannot be explained. It takes its root from the Latin word ‘mysterium’ and from the ancient Greek word ‘musterion,’ meaning a secret or secret rite. Iniquity from its root word ‘anomia’ (in Greek) means illegality, i.e. violation of law or wickedness: transgression of the law, unrighteousness or lawlessness. Therefore, the mystery of iniquity is a system of lawlessness of which believers are warned and should watch out for.

The mystery of iniquity refers to the pervasive influence of lawlessness in the world, fostering a global rebellion against God (Matthew 24:12; 2 Timothy 3:1-4). It seeks to control people, systems, and finances (Genesis 11:4) and manifests as a complex network that has infiltrated politics, entertainment, sports, education, religion, media, and more (Romans 1:21-22). It is also revealed through seductive spirits and the doctrines of demons (2 Timothy 3:13; 1 Timothy 4:1), resulting in sinful behaviour and diabolic practices among humanity (Acts 8:22-23; Matthew 23:28).

Iniquity primarily affects the inner character (Mark 7:21-23) and reflects a deliberate desire to distort God’s holy standard (Jude 4). It drives people to twist God’s word for their own purpose (Titus 1:11). Ultimately, this movement of lawlessness will culminate in the appearance of the Antichrist. Though his spirit is already active in the world, it is currently restrained, preventing humanity from reaching the full extent of its potential evil (2 Thessalonians 2:7-8; 1John 4:3).
In a world filled with lawlessness, believers are called to:

i: Guard their hearts diligently and continually (Joel 2:13; Proverbs 4:23).
Confess and repent of all known sin to receive God’s forgiveness (1 John 1:9; Acts 3:19).
Resist conformity to the world and faithfully obey God’s commandments (Romans 12:2; Deuteronomy 11:22).
Watch, pray, and seek renewal of heart from the Lord (Matthew 26:41; Psalm 51:10).
Clothe themselves with the new nature and be continually renewed by the Holy Spirit (Colossians 3:10; Titus 3:5).
Turn away from iniquity and remove the old patterns of sin (2 Timothy 2:19; 1Corinthians 5:7).
Purify themselves and maintain holiness in life and conduct (2 Timothy 2:21; Ecclesiastes 9:8).

b.x: Believers must know that the spirit of lawlessness is operating in the world presently, and they must ensure that they keep the profession of their faith to the end.
